General

As part of its Accessibility Plan, Saudia has designated a senior manager to accept, review, and act on feedback:

Manager – Policies, Governance & Compliance
Saudia
Head Office, Khaledia District
PO Box 620, Loc 130
Jeddah, Saudi Arabia 21235

All feedback anonymous or not, comments and suggestions on our Accessibility Plan, as well as requests for a copy of our Accessibility Plan, feedback process or progress report in various alternate formats, are now accepted through various channels:

Online form:
For added convenience, an online feedback form has been made available by Saudia for submission of comments and suggestions regarding accessibility. However, the corporate website is currently undergoing revamp in overall layout and the link will be restored by July or August 2026.

Information and Communication Technologies (ICT)

Saudia’s website is managed using the latest Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.0 Level AA Success Criteria to make it accessible to a worldwide audience, including end-users with disabilities. We strive to deliver the best website experience to users by constantly improving and upgrading the system, irrespective of technology or physical barriers.

Saudia’s web accessibility compliance is further covered in its Accessibility Statement. The corporate website is currently undergoing revamp in overall layout and the link will be restored by July or August 2026.

An internal Task Force, which will assess and evaluate Saudia’s on-going accessibility initiatives has been organized.

In-terminal announcements are in both audio and visual formats, which is already being practiced in all Saudia gateways in the USA and Canada.

Third-party accessibility audit resources had been studied, with a number of service providers engaged and proposals obtained. However, due to budget constraints, the initiative has been put on hold for now.

Communication other than ICT

Saudia has integrated systems that provide information at different customer touchpoints, available in audio, visual and other alternative formats. These systems have been reviewed and updated and deemed in compliance with ATPDR.

  • The setting up of Teletypewriter/test display device (TTY) has been studied but concrete action has been postponed due to budget limitations. This has been discussed with the outsourced Call Center and will be taken up again in the Fourth Quarter 2026.
  • In-person interaction – Our ground agents and cabin crew undergo sensitivity training, among other things, to ensure they always communicate with our customers, especially those with disabilities, to see if they need assistance.
  • Aircraft – Saudia has ordered new aircraft from Boeing and Airbus but delivery is not yet imminent. The plan is to provide English and Arabic braille passenger safety feature cards as well as large print, and braille formats of the Air Passenger Protection Regulation (APPR), which will be made available upon request.

Procurement of goods, services, and facilities

Saudia has reviewed its procurement procedures to enhance compliance with all regulatory requirements of countries it operates in. Accessibility standards are, whenever possible, built into procurement processes and accessibility criteria considered when purchasing new goods and services, to make sure deliverables have accessibility features.

Goods and services not in compliance with ATPDR accessibility standards will require clear justifications to be provided and documented. Work is currently on-going but documentation is pending due to workloads and shortage of staff.

Likewise, for suppliers failing to meet the accessibility standards required by procedures, Saudia will determine if the supplier offers goods or services that are flexible and have built-in features or functions to provide accessibility to the most number of users.

Design and delivery of programs and services

Saudia’s IT Department and web development teams confirm that Saudia complies with (WCAG) 2.0 AA and meets the Canadian Transportation Agency’s Accessible Transportation for Persons with Disabilities Regulations, as well as the U.S. Department of Transportation Ruling under 14 CFR Part 382, Nondiscrimination on the Basis of Disability in Air Travel. Furthermore, we are working towards WCAG 2.1 AA conformance to meet the Canadian and U.S. requirements and the requirements of the European Union Web Accessibility Directive. More work on this is expected in the First Quarter of 2027.

Saudia is still in discussions with shortlisted web accessibility consultants to help test, develop, remediate, and maintain our website in-line with the latest Web Content Accessibility Guidelines. The current crisis in the Middle East – Saudia’s home market, has led to cost challenges and this program has been put on hold and will be done internally for now.

Due to the current crisis, training for frontline Saudia personnel on accessibility requirements has been put on hold for now but planning will resume once the political situation has stabilized and business is back to normal.

Transportation

Saudia continues to comply with accessibility regulations of countries it operates in, to include the Accessible Transportation for Persons with Disabilities Regulations, in which Saudia is considered a large carrier required to comply with Parts 1 and 2 of this regulation. Furthermore, Saudia is compliant with the U.S. Department of Transportation 14 CFR Part 382.

The Built Environment

  • Airport lounges – Saudia has confirmed its compliance with accessibility standards, providing open seating, and accessible lavatories in its airport lounges – both in its own home base in Jeddah, Saudi Arabia, or the airport lounges it contracts with in the airports it operates to in Canada, USA and other cities worldwide.
  • Aircraft fleet – Saudia’s aircraft have on-board wheelchairs and wheelchair accessible lavatories on selected aircraft. Certain aircraft types have passenger seats with moveable armrests, which are placed throughout the aircraft.

Provisions of CTA accessibility-related regulations

As a large carrier under Canadian Transportation Agency regulations, Saudia complies, to the best of its ability, with provisions of the Accessible Transportation for Persons with Disabilities Regulations (SOR/2019 244) contained in parts 1 and 2 applicable to foreign carriers.

Feedback Information

No meaningful or actionable feedback has yet been received on Saudia’s communication channels dedicated to accessibility. More comments and feedback are expected as its Accessibility Plan generates more exposure to its customer base.

Consultations

Saudia formed a Task Force composed of managers and staff with wide ranging expertise to help on the implementation of its Accessibility Plan.

It has communicated with disability advocacy groups to ensure constant feedback and interaction with relevant groups and organizations. Active, working engagements with such groups cannot be implemented at the moment due to financial constraints brought about by the current conflict in the Middle East.

Saudia will continue its commitment to developing employee and customer service policies that comply with Accessible Transportation for Persons with Disabilities Regulations (ATPDR).

Further development of policies and procedures related to accessibility – in consultation with persons with disabilities, however, will have to wait until after the crisis in the Middle East has abated.

External consultations

Saudia has started discussions with Open Doors Organization, a US 501(c)(3) public charity non-profit with a mission to make goods and services accessible to people with disabilities in travel, tourism, and transportation. These discussions include consultations to review and develop its training programs for sensitivity and proper handling and communication with passengers with disabilities. Due to budget constraints, formal working relations have been postponed until early next year.

Internal consultations

Saudia still plans to undertake efforts to consult employees who either have friends and relatives who have disabilities or are themselves disabled. This initiative is currently on hold due to operational priorities related to mitigating the negative impact of the regional conflict on airline operations and financial health.

Saudia further commits to regular company communication, as part of its Transformation Program, to invite insights and input on various issues regarding accessibility with relevant discussions to be featured on the e-staff and transformation portals.

Meantime, Saudia will continue to identify and provide solutions to accessibility challenges, including:

  • Reviewing and revising policies and procedures to remove obstacles to accessibility in coordination with managers, supervisors, and employees.
  • Determining employee accessibility requirements throughout their employment.
  • Providing the latest technology and assistive devices in anticipation of accessibility needs when they arise.
